theme: Woe to those who go to Egypt; the highway of holiness
readingInstruction: Read Isaiah 31:1-35:10. The woes continue against reliance on Egypt, but then chapters 32 to 35 move toward a glorious future. Read chapter 35 slowly, as a picture of the transformed world.
settingTheScene: The crisis with Assyria is at its height. Hezekiah’s advisors continue to look to Egypt for horses and chariots. Isaiah warns them against it, and then describes a righteous king, a poured-out Spirit, a coming judgment on Edom, and the joyful return of the redeemed along “the highway of holiness.” Chapters 34 and 35 close the first half of Isaiah with a stark contrast between judgment and joy.
observation: “Woe to those who go down to Egypt for help and rely on horses, who trust in chariots because they are many… but do not look to the Holy One of Israel” (31:1).
“The Egyptians are man, and not God, and their horses are flesh, and not spirit” (31:3).
“Behold, a king will reign in righteousness, and princes will rule in justice” (32:1).
“Until the Spirit is poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness becomes a fruitful field” (32:15).
“The effect of righteousness will be peace, and the result of righteousness, quietness and trust forever” (32:17).
“O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you” (33:2).
“For the LORD is our judge; the LORD is our lawgiver; the LORD is our king; he will save us” (33:22).
“And a highway shall be there, and it shall be called the Way of Holiness” (35:8).
interpretation:
The main sin of chapter 31 is stated plainly: trusting in horses and chariots rather than in the Holy One of Israel. Isaiah’s contrast is memorable: “The Egyptians are man, and not God, and their horses are flesh, and not spirit.” Whatever human power we trust in is limited by its own nature. The LORD of hosts will fight for Jerusalem like a lion over its prey or like birds hovering. He will protect and deliver.

Chapter 32 opens with a promise of a righteous king and a time when people will see clearly. It also speaks to the complacent women of the city, who will be shaken from their ease. But then, “until the Spirit is poured upon us from on high.” This is a promise of the Spirit’s coming and of a transformation of the land. The result is justice, righteousness, peace, and security. These flow from God’s Spirit.

Chapter 33 contains a prayer, “O LORD, be gracious to us; we wait for you,” and then the stunning reversal of the Assyrian threat. The enemy who dealt treacherously will be dealt with. Then the prophet asks who can live with the consuming fire, and answers: he who walks righteously and speaks uprightly. And the chapter ends with a great statement: “The LORD is our judge; the LORD is our lawgiver; the LORD is our king; he will save us.”

Chapter 34 is the dark side, a judgment on the nations, symbolized by Edom. And chapter 35 is the bright side. It is a poem of transformation. The desert blossoms. The weak hands are strengthened. The eyes of the blind are opened, the ears of the deaf unstopped, the lame leap like a deer, and the mute sing. A highway is built, the Way of Holiness. The unclean shall not pass over it, but the redeemed shall walk there. “The ransomed of the LORD shall return and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy shall be upon their heads.” It is the vision of salvation as a return home.
connection: When John the Baptist’s disciples asked Jesus if he was the one, Jesus answered by pointing to the signs of Isaiah 35: the blind see, the lame walk, the deaf hear (Matthew 11:2-5). Acts 2:17 quotes Joel on the pouring out of the Spirit, and Acts 2 shows its fulfillment. Jesus said, “I am the way” (John 14:6). Hebrews 12:12 echoes Isaiah 35:3. Revelation 21:4 says sorrow and sighing will flee away.
application:
Identify one “horse and chariot” you tend to trust, whether money, connections, or skills. Place it under God’s care.

Pray for the Spirit to be “poured out from on high” on your church and community.

Strengthen a weak hand this week by encouraging someone who is struggling.
prayerPrompts: Confess where you trust horses and chariots.
Ask God to pour out his Spirit on his people.
Thank him that he makes a highway of holiness for his redeemed.
